newsitem.title: USA: CSX, Conrail merger seen good for grain shippers.
newsitem.headline: CSX, Conrail merger seen good for grain shippers.

text.p: A proposed rail merger between CSX Corp and Conrail Inc was viewed as beneficial by some southeastern U.S. cash grain merchants while others warn it could result in higher freight rates.
"It's going to make a bigger market for shippers and receivers, but any time two competitors merge, you run the risk of higher freight rates," one southeastern cash grain merchant said.
CSX and Conrail, two rail companies that serve eastern U.S. markets, said Thursday the two would merge, leaving only Norfolk Southern Corp as a competitor, sources said.
Although higher freight rates could result from the merger, most industry observers said it was unlikely that any immediate rate rate changes would occur.

"In the long term, I think it's good for the grain industry," said Stephen Norris, manager of grain trading for Southern States Cooperative in Richmond, VA. "It will create more efficiency and open up markets to people."

Grain shippers in the Ohio Valley were seen as beneficiaries of the proposed merger because it will grant them access to CSX's strong base of feedmills in North Carolina and Virginia, one grain merchant said.
"There's been a lot of conversation about a merger between someone and Conrail," one southern broker said. "I think people were surprised it was CSX and not someone else."
The proposed merger would create a 22-state transportation network covering 29,645 miles from Chicago to New York to Miami, the rail companies said in a news release.

In response to the news, Norfolk Southern issued a statement Tuesday that said such a merger "raises serious concerns" and had "very significant implications for the nation's transportation system and for the shipping public."
